title: Leadership priority canvas — Q2 commitments & townline script
content:
Purpose: capture a single canvas that leaders can use to align, brief execs, and feed the all-hands narrative. This is intentionally concise — think: one screen for the CEO + five supporting slides.

Topline thesis (one line): Focus Q2 on shipping predictable inference economics and fail-safe reliability so customers can migrate from pilot to production.

Priority pillars (short):
1) Serve: SLA + latency guardrails (predictability) — reduce 95p latency by 15% for hosted API peak windows; formalize fallback tiers.
2) Scale: Dedicated capacity ramp and onboarding — secure two pilot enterprise Dedicated contracts and 80% of Reserved capacity filled.
3) Trust: Private deployment readiness (VPC/HSM + audits) — complete SOC-type checklist and two customer POCs.

Why these (context bullets):
- Market: customers increasingly choose vendors on inference economics and predictable latency, not just model quality.
- Sales signal: multiple mid-market accounts paused until Dedicated SLAs and Private compliance artifacts are available.
- Risk: without predictable throughput tooling, unit costs spike under burst patterns and engineers avoid productionizing features.

Draft high-level OKRs (for exec review) — objective then KRs (rough):
- Objective A: Make Redwood the fastest, most predictable hosted inference platform for PLG flows.
  - KR A1: 95th percentile generation latency down 15% across top-10 workloads by end of Q2.
  - KR A2: Automatic prefix/KV cache hit-rate >= 35% for steady-state web traffic.
  - KR A3: Launch model-variant fallback runway with documented performance profiles for 5 model families.
- Objective B: Convert pilot users into Dedicated customers with predictable economics.
  - KR B1: Close 2 Dedicated pilot contracts (>= $200k ARR each) and onboard them to production.
  - KR B2: Reach 80% utilization of reserved-capacity pool without violating latency SLOs.
  - KR B3: Publish a cost playbook (benchmarks + best practices) for customers and SREs.
- Objective C: Enterprise trust and private deployments (compliance).
  - KR C1: Complete audit-readiness checklist and pass a tabletop for at least one regulated scenario.
  - KR C2: Ship a private-deploy starter kit (VPC + KMS templates) and 2 POCs.
  - KR C3: Add encryption-at-rest + HSM integration docs and runbook.

Success metrics & signals to monitor (ops-ready):
- Token throughput per GPU (median) and cost per 1M tokens.
- 95p latency per route/model and per-region.
- Cache hit-rates, average batch size, and cold-start frequency.
- Customer onboarding velocity for Dedicated (days to first production call).
- Number of policy incidents or security audit findings.

All-hands narrative (10-minute slot) — sketch:
- 0:00–1:00: Quick state: three one-liners for progress vs Q1.
- 1:00–4:00: The problem we’re solving (predictable economics + trust) — three concrete customer stories (one PLG scale, one Dedicated pilot, one private POC).
- 4:00–7:00: Our Q2 commitments (show the three pillars, headline KRs).
- 7:00–9:00: What to expect from teams (calls to action and micro-asks: instrument metrics, prioritize eviction-safe batching, help with sales POC playbooks).
- 9:00–10:00: Risks & contingency (what success looks like and the fallback plan).

Townline talking points for execs (short script):
- "We learned from recent pilots that customers choke on unpredictability more than absolute latency numbers. This quarter we lock in predictability — it's our defensive moat."
- "We will be transparent: for two weeks after a Dedicated launch we’ll run a shared dashboard with the customer on throughput and billing signals."
- "If any customer experiences repeated SLA breaches, we have an automated rollback to a lower-capacity but higher-availability tier and a customer remediation flow (we'll share the runbook)."

Contingency scenarios (decision rules — quick):
- Scenario 1: If 95p latency increases > 20% month-over-month for top-10 tenants — trigger emergency task force (SRE + serving runtime + account lead).
  - Immediate action: enable model-variant fallback and increase logging/trace collection to 6x retention for affected tenants.
- Scenario 2: If Dedicated pilot fails to meet baseline throughput in two weeks — offer short-term credit + rollback to hosted with uplifted support while we remediate config.
- Scenario 3: If Private POC hits compliance gap (audit finding) — pause new private signups and route prospective customers to a waiting list + weekly remediation updates.

Operational play (what teams do this week — checklist):
- Serving runtime: finish end-to-end test for auto-fallback pipeline (owner: Marcus, ETA: 2025-03-18).
- Console: add a per-tenant latency SLO dashboard and SLA heatmap (owner: Priya, ETA: 2025-03-21).
- Sales/SE: prepare two Dedicated pilot contracts with clearly defined acceptance criteria (owner: Owen, ETA: 2025-03-25).
- Security: finalize HSM-runbook and KMS templates for private deployments (owner: Taylor, ETA: 2025-03-28).
- Product: finalize model-variant catalog and verified perf profiles (owner: Dina, ETA: 2025-03-22).

Communications plan (short):
- Week 1: Exec briefing (walk the canvas) + leadership alignment session.
- Week 2: Publish Q2 commitments to company (short email + Confluence one-pager + townline slot).
- Ongoing: Weekly progress micro-updates in #company-townline and an internal dashboard.

Open questions / forks (notes to self and execs):
- How strict should KR thresholds be for customer-facing comms? (tight targets risk repeated public misses; softer thresholds risk diluted ambition) — decision needed by 2025-03-19.
- Do we surface a per-customer cost index in the console (privacy + support implications)?
- Should we advertise fallback tiers in public docs or only share with customers under NDA?

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: We under-provision Dedicated fleets and overload shared capacity at peak.
  - Mitigation: conservative ramping policy + auto-burst limit per account + visibility alerts.
- Risk: POCs reveal gaps in compliance posture.
  - Mitigation: stop new private signups until core checklist passes; allocate SRE time for audit remediation.
- Risk: Customers misinterpret fallback as downgrade in quality.
  - Mitigation: explicit messaging + integration tests that compare fallback outputs for regressions.

Decision log (items we need to close in next 2 weeks):
- Approve public-facing KR framing (tight vs pragmatic) — owner: CEO office.
- Greenlight 2 enterprise Dedicated pilot credits ($50k each cap) — owner: Finance + RevOps.
- Prioritize HSM integration in Q2 roadmap — owner: CTO.

Appendix: quick roll-call of supporting artifacts to attach before final exec deck:
- SLA glossary and SLO measurement guide (Confluence link).
- Dedicated contract template and acceptance criteria (DOCX).
- Private deployment runbook + KMS/HSM templates (GitHub repo link).
- Example customer onboarding timeline (sheet: cadence and tasks).

Quick TODO (for this doc):
- [ ] Fold in Marcus' latency experiment numbers and update KR A1 (due 2025-03-12).
- [ ] Add SE playbook bullets from Owen (due 2025-03-14).
- [ ] Draft townline speaking notes for CEO and Head of Product (due 2025-03-16).

Notes to self: keep the canvas short and executable. Avoid 10-objective lists — pick 3 things we can show progress on weekly. This doc is a synthesis — more detail belongs in the team-level execution plans.
